phases.name: Research Foundations & Lab Onboarding
phases.theme: scientific computing, problem formulation, literature search & applied statistics
phases.purpose: Become a reliable contributor who can enter a lab, find a gap, and make defensible claims.

phases.name: Data Curation & Modeling Paradigms
phases.theme: domain datasets, classical ML, deep learning, computer vision, graphs and sequence models
phases.purpose: Turn real-world data and model architectures into testable research baselines.

phases.name: Generative Models & Experimental Science
phases.theme: generative modeling, controlled ablations, fair benchmarks and scaled experimental systems
phases.purpose: Design controlled experiments and scale them far enough to reveal meaningful behavior.

phases.name: Scaled Systems, Trustworthy AI & Alignment
phases.theme: foundation models, interpretability, robustness, fairness and alignment for high-impact domains
phases.purpose: Study powerful models critically and evaluate their behavior, risks, and limits.

phases.name: Cross-Disciplinary Research
phases.purpose: Translate research questions across disciplines and lead collaborative studies.

phases.name: Thesis & Research Portfolio
phases.theme: thesis-grade evidence, reproducibility, and research communication
phases.purpose: Own a substantial study from protocol through evidence and portfolio.

phases.name: Publishing, Defense & Careers
phases.theme: journals, conferences, peer review, viva, interviews, and research careers
phases.purpose: Publish, defend, and carry research into academic or industrial employment.

levels.title: Computing, Python & Learning Habits
levels.scope: Build the everyday computing, Python, communication, and study habits needed to learn data science without relying on copy-paste tutorials.
levels.prereqStated: None; designed for a complete beginner

modules.name: Computer and Command-Line Foundations

objectives.text: Explain how files, folders, programs, memory, and networks work together.
Navigate a terminal, create files, inspect processes, and read error messages.
Use a Linux shell, SSH, environment variables, and a remote notebook safely.
Organize research notes, downloads, datasets, and code with predictable names.
Protect credentials, recognize unsafe commands, and keep private data out of repositories.
Describe licenses, attribution, accessibility, and responsible use of AI tools.
Create a reproducible environment file and record the exact interpreter, package, and operating-system versions.
Use small tests, clear error messages, and a research log so another learner can reproduce the same result.

modules.mentalModel: The command line is a precise laboratory instrument, not a mysterious black box.
modules.tryIt: Create a small project folder, document every command in a lab notebook, and reproduce the setup on a second machine.
modules.outcome: You can work safely in a computing environment and explain what your tools are doing.
modules.evidence: Create a small project folder, document every command in a lab notebook, and reproduce the setup on a second machine.

modules.name: Python Programming for Data Work

objectives.text: Use variables, strings, numbers, booleans, conditionals, loops, and functions.
Break a task into small functions and test each function with simple examples.
Work with lists, dictionaries, sets, tuples, CSV files, and JSON documents.
Handle missing files and malformed input with clear, user-facing errors.
Import standard-library modules, read tracebacks, and debug with a small reproducible example.
Use type hints and docstrings to make beginner code understandable to collaborators.
Write a script that loads a dataset, computes summary statistics, and saves a report.
Run the same script from a clean terminal and record its inputs and outputs.
Separate configuration, code, data, and generated artifacts so an experiment can be rerun without manual edits.
Add a smoke test and a machine-readable result summary to every small research script.

modules.mentalModel: Programming is the practice of turning an explicit procedure into repeatable instructions.
modules.tryIt: Build a command-line dataset summary tool with tests for empty, missing, and malformed inputs.
modules.outcome: You can write, run, debug, and explain small Python programs for data tasks.
modules.evidence: Build a command-line dataset summary tool with tests for empty, missing, and malformed inputs.

modules.name: Git, Documentation & Deliberate Learning

objectives.text: Initialize a Git repository, make focused commits, inspect diffs, and recover from mistakes.
Use branches and pull requests to ask for review without losing working code.
Write a README with purpose, setup, usage, limitations, and an example result.
Turn a confusing error or experiment into a concise issue containing evidence and a question.
Plan weekly study blocks, use retrieval practice, and maintain a questions-and-evidence log.
Distinguish understanding a concept from recognizing a familiar code pattern.

modules.mentalModel: A research career compounds small, documented improvements rather than isolated bursts of motivation.
modules.tryIt: Publish a beginner-friendly repository with a README, changelog, issue, and three meaningful commits.
modules.outcome: You can learn in public, collaborate with version control, and communicate technical work clearly.
modules.evidence: Publish a beginner-friendly repository with a README, changelog, issue, and three meaningful commits.

modules.name: Research Environments and Experiment Records

objectives.text: Create a locked environment file and record interpreter, package, hardware, and operating-system versions.
Separate source code, raw data, derived data, configurations, logs, and generated figures.
Keep a dated research log with hypotheses, commands, decisions, failures, and next actions.
Use deterministic seeds and machine-readable configuration files for small experiments.
Add smoke tests, input validation, and a clean-run checklist to a research repository.
Re-run a result from a fresh environment and compare the output with a stored reference.

modules.mentalModel: Reproducibility starts with ordinary habits long before a paper is written.
modules.tryIt: Recreate one analysis on a second machine using only the repository and its setup instructions.
modules.outcome: You can create a research environment another person can inspect and reproduce.
modules.evidence: Recreate one analysis on a second machine using only the repository and its setup instructions.

modules.name: Data Literacy and Scientific Communication

objectives.text: Inspect tabular data, missing values, units, distributions, and obvious collection errors.
Make a small figure with a caption that states what the data supports and what it does not.
Explain a result to a technical peer and a non-specialist without changing its meaning.

modules.mentalModel: A clear artifact is part of the evidence, not decoration added at the end.
modules.tryIt: Turn one dataset summary into a notebook, a figure, and a five-sentence research briefing.
modules.outcome: You can communicate beginner analysis with accurate scope and limitations.
modules.evidence: Turn one dataset summary into a notebook, a figure, and a five-sentence research briefing.

levels.title: Mathematics for Data Science
levels.scope: Develop the algebra, functions, calculus, and linear algebra intuition required to understand models instead of treating libraries as magic.

modules.name: Algebra, Functions & Logarithms

objectives.text: Manipulate equations, ratios, inequalities, powers, logarithms, and summations.
Read a function as an input-output rule and interpret slope, curvature, and scale.
Use units, orders of magnitude, and dimensional checks to catch impossible results.
Use dimensional analysis, numerical checks, and visualizations to catch incorrect derivations before they enter an experiment.
Connect each mathematical object to a modeling decision, an optimization behavior, and a measurable research consequence.

modules.mentalModel: Mathematical notation is a compact language for describing relationships that code can execute.
modules.tryIt: Implement and plot linear, polynomial, exponential, and logarithmic functions, then explain where each is useful.
modules.outcome: You can translate common quantitative statements between words, equations, plots, and Python.
modules.evidence: Implement and plot linear, polynomial, exponential, and logarithmic functions, then explain where each is useful.

modules.name: Linear Algebra & Geometry

objectives.text: Represent vectors, matrices, tensors, basis changes, dot products, norms, and projections.
Derive matrix multiplication dimensions and use geometric language to explain distance and similarity.
Implement a small neural layer with NumPy and verify it against hand-calculated examples.
Use dimensional analysis, numerical checks, and visualizations to catch incorrect derivations before they enter an experiment.
Connect each mathematical object to a modeling decision, an optimization behavior, and a measurable research consequence.

modules.mentalModel: Most machine-learning computation is geometry performed efficiently on batches of examples.
modules.tryIt: Build a visual notebook for projections, least squares, principal components, and cosine similarity.
modules.outcome: You can follow the linear-algebra operations behind regression, embeddings, and neural networks.
modules.evidence: Build a visual notebook for projections, least squares, principal components, and cosine similarity.

modules.name: Derivatives and Optimization Intuition

objectives.text: Interpret derivatives, partial derivatives, gradients, Jacobians, and Hessians.
Apply the chain rule to a small computation graph and check gradients numerically.
Explain learning rate, local minima, conditioning, and why normalization affects optimization.
Use dimensional analysis, numerical checks, and visualizations to catch incorrect derivations before they enter an experiment.
Connect each mathematical object to a modeling decision, an optimization behavior, and a measurable research consequence.

modules.mentalModel: Training adjusts parameters in directions that reduce a chosen error surface.
modules.tryIt: Implement gradient descent for a one-variable and two-variable function and compare step sizes.
modules.outcome: You can explain and verify the calculus used to train predictive models.
modules.evidence: Implement gradient descent for a one-variable and two-variable function and compare step sizes.

modules.name: Matrix Calculus and Automatic Differentiation

objectives.text: Express Jacobians, Hessians, vector-Jacobian products, and matrix derivatives with correct shapes.
Verify an automatic-differentiation result with finite differences and diagnose numerical error.

modules.mentalModel: Shape checks and independent derivatives are mathematical unit tests.
modules.tryIt: Derive and verify gradients for a two-layer network with a scalar loss.
modules.outcome: You can inspect the calculus behind a training implementation.
modules.evidence: Derive and verify gradients for a two-layer network with a scalar loss.

modules.name: Optimization Algorithms and Numerical Stability

objectives.text: Compare batch, stochastic, and mini-batch gradient descent under different conditioning and step sizes.
Explain exploding updates, vanishing gradients, normalization, regularization, and stable log-domain computation.

modules.mentalModel: Optimization is an experiment whose assumptions and failure modes must be measured.
modules.tryIt: Compare optimizers on a controlled loss surface and report convergence, sensitivity, and failure cases.
modules.outcome: You can connect mathematical assumptions to optimization behavior.
modules.evidence: Compare optimizers on a controlled loss surface and report convergence, sensitivity, and failure cases.

modules.name: Capstone: Mathematical Model Notebook

objectives.text: Derive ordinary least squares from a clearly stated objective and assumptions.
Implement the solution with NumPy and compare it with a trusted library.
Include plots, dimensional checks, numerical-gradient checks, and a plain-language explanation.

modules.finalResult: A mathematical notebook that connects equations, geometry, optimization, code, and model behavior.
modules.evidence: A mathematical notebook that connects equations, geometry, optimization, code, and model behavior.

levels.assessmentStandard: Complete the objectives, submit the evidence artifact, and defend the capstone result with limitations.
levels.careerSignal: Can explain the quantitative foundations of model behavior.
completionOutcomes: You can translate common quantitative statements between words, equations, plots, and Python.
